results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Kaskazi Everyday Account has a monthly fee of **KES 250**. Kaskazi Bank works out at the end of each calendar month whether the fee applies for that month. If either of the two waivers below applies, you pay nothing for that month. If neither applies, KES 250 is taken from the account at the end of the month.

You can avoid it in either of these ways:

- **Have your salary paid in:** The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account.
- **Keep a high average balance:** The KES 250 monthly fee on the Kaskazi Everyday Account is also waived for any month in which your average balance is KES 50,000 or more. Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month.

You only need one of these. If you are self-employed or paid in cash, you won't qualify for the salary waiver, but you can still use the average balance waiver.

results.question: what does 'up to 50 days interest free' actually mean? do I get 50 days on everything I buy with the credit card?
results.answer:
No, you don't get 50 days on everything. The Kaskazi Credit Card gives you up to 50 days without interest on purchases. The interest-free period runs from the day you make a purchase to the payment due date of the statement that purchase appears on.

A purchase made on the first day of a statement period waits the longest before it is due, so it gets the full 50 days. A purchase made on the last day of a statement period gets the fewest days. In the bank's example, a statement period runs from 1 May to 31 May with a due date of 20 June, so a purchase on 1 May gets 50 days, one on 15 May gets 36 days, and one on 31 May gets 20 days.

The interest-free period also applies only when you pay your full statement balance by the payment due date. It doesn't apply to cash advances, which are charged interest from the day you take the cash.

results.question: how much is the monthly fee on everyday account? and can i avoid paying it
results.answer:

results.answer:

Here is what I can tell you now. If you held a joint Kaskazi Everyday Account, the money in the joint Kaskazi Everyday Account belongs to the surviving holder or holders, who can keep using the account. Kaskazi Bank will need to see the death certificate.

If he had a Kaskazi Personal Loan, a family member or the person handling the estate should tell us as soon as they can, at a branch or through the assistant, and give us a copy of the death certificate.

I can only see the accounts and loans in your own name, so I can't see his account from here. A colleague has been alerted and will reply in this chat, usually within about 5 minutes between 7:00 am and 10:00 pm. They can take you through the steps for his account. results.question: Is there a monthly fee on the Everyday Account?
results.answer:
Yes. The Kaskazi Everyday Account has a monthly fee of KES 250. You do not pay it in any month when your salary is paid into the account, or when your average balance for the month is KES 50,000 or more. If neither applies, KES 250 is taken from the account at the end of the month.

The average balance is measured across the month, not the lowest point. A balance that dips below KES 50,000 for a few days can still average KES 50,000 or more.
